issues.title: Using assert instead of XCTAssert
issues.description: The rule requires test methods to use assertions from the XCTest framework (XCTAssert family), but standard Swift assert() functions were used instead of XCTAssertTrue()
issues.rule_name: Test Classes Must Use XCTest Framework with Proper Structure

issues.title: Incorrect tearDown order in StoriesFeedDiffableDataSourceTests
issues.description: The tearDown method calls super.tearDown() before cleaning up test dependencies. In XCTest, super.tearDown() should be called after cleaning up resources to ensure proper cleanup order. Calling super.tearDown() first can cause issues when the parent class attempts to access or clean up resources that are about to be deallocated. The DependencyHelperMock().reset() and collectionView/diffableDataSource cleanup should happen before calling the parent's tearDown to prevent potential crashes or state inconsistencies between tests.

issues.title: Test state cleanup after super.tearDown in RatingPromptManagerTests
issues.description: The tearDown method calls super.tearDown() before cleaning up test-specific state (prefs, subject, userDefaults, etc.). This is problematic because XCTest's tearDown should clean up test-specific resources before calling super.tearDown(). By calling super.tearDown() first, any state or resources that should be cleaned up might leak into subsequent tests or cause undefined behavior. Specifically, calling prefs.clearAll() and subject.reset() after super.tearDown() violates the expected tearDown lifecycle and can lead to test isolation issues where one test's state affects another.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
override func tearDown() async throws {
        try await super.tearDown()
        prefs.clearAll()
        subject.reset()
        prefs = nil
        logger = nil
        urlOpenerSpy = nil
        userDefaults = nil
        crashTracker = nil
        subject = nil
    }

issues.title: Missing @MainActor annotation in EditBookmarkViewModelTests
issues.description: The EditBookmarkViewModelTests class is missing the @MainActor annotation that was added in the PR for Swift 6 concurrency compliance. This test class uses UI components (UITableView) and interacts with MainActor-isolated types. Without the @MainActor annotation, the tests may experience data races or undefined behavior when accessing MainActor-isolated properties, particularly since the setUp and tearDown methods are now async and the test methods interact with UI components. This violates Swift 6 concurrency requirements and can lead to runtime crashes or unpredictable test behavior.

issues.title: UI-related test lifecycle method not annotated with @MainActor
issues.description: This test creates/configures a UIViewController in setUp, which is UI work. Rule 9 requires UI-related code to be annotated with @MainActor (either on the class or the method). The modified setUp() signature is not annotated and the class is not marked @MainActor in the diff.
issues.rule_name: UI-Related Code Must Be Annotated with @MainActor

issues.title: Mock class not marked final
issues.description: Per Rule 12, classes that are not intended for subclassing should be marked `final`. This mock type appears to be a concrete test helper and is modified in this PR, but remains non-final.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31130 - Refactor FXIOS-14344 [Swift 6 migration] Fixing warnings in unit tests

structured_output.summary:
This is a test-only Swift 6 migration. It converts about 20 XCTestCase suites from `setUp()`/`tearDown()` to `async throws` overrides with explicit `try await super.setUp()` and `super.tearDown()` calls, adds `@MainActor` to several suites, and adjusts mocks (`MockTabQueue` closure signature, `@unchecked Sendable` on `MockUserNotificationCenter`, `final` on a challenge sender). The async lifecycle conversion and the TabQueue signature fix are sound and match the protocol in `Storage/Queue.swift`.

Two changes are problematic. In `NotificationManagerTests`, `XCTAssertTrue` was replaced with Swift's `assert`, which does not record XCTest failures and is compiled out of optimized builds. In `EditBookmarkViewModelTests`, the class-level `@MainActor` was removed even though the tests call the `@MainActor`-isolated `selectFolder`, which is likely to add isolation errors or warnings rather than remove them. Both problems are in a PR whose purpose is to clean up concurrency warnings.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `EditBookmarkViewModelTests` isolation change can reintroduce the warnings this PR is meant to remove, and the `NotificationManagerTests` change weakens a test so it can no longer fail cleanly. Both fixes are small. The lifecycle conversion across the other suites looks correct.

architecture.overview:
This PR only touches the unit test target (`firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests`). Production code is unchanged. Each XCTestCase sets up shared state in `setUp` and calls `DependencyHelperMock().bootstrapDependencies()`, a non-isolated helper class in `DependencyInjection/DependencyHelperMock.swift`, and calls `reset()` in tear-down. Production types such as `EditBookmarkViewModel` and `NotificationManager` expose a mix of `@MainActor` and `@Sendable` APIs, and the test mocks must match those signatures.

The PR moves the touched suites onto the async XCTest lifecycle (`override func setUp() async throws` / `tearDown() async throws` with explicit `try await super` calls). It also adds or removes `@MainActor` on suites so test code runs in the same isolation domain as the types it exercises. The mock changes align test doubles with protocol signatures; for example, `MockTabQueue.getQueuedTabs` now matches the `@MainActor @Sendable @escaping` closure declared in `Storage/Queue.swift`.
steps: Entry point: XCTest runs each suite's `setUp`, which is now `async throws` and calls `DependencyHelperMock().bootstrapDependencies()` to inject mocked dependencies. That helper is not `@MainActor`, so calling it from a `@MainActor` suite is safe.
Lifecycle change: most of the diff converts `setUp`/`tearDown` to `async throws` and makes `super` calls explicit. Placement of the `super` calls varies between suites.

Isolation change: `@MainActor` is added to StoriesFeedDiffableDataSourceTests, EditBookmarkDataSourceTests, MainMenuViewControllerTests, MicrosurveyViewControllerTests and NativeErrorPageViewControllerTests, and removed from EditBookmarkViewModelTests. That removal needs a second look because the suite calls the `@MainActor` `selectFolder`.
Mock alignment: `MockTabQueue.getQueuedTabs` matches the protocol signature, `MockUserNotificationCenter` is marked `@unchecked Sendable`, and `MockURLAuthenticationChallengeSender` is made `final`.
Assertion change: `NotificationManagerTests.testRequestAuthorization` swaps XCTest assertions for Swift `assert`, which changes how failures are reported.

diagrams.title: Test suite lifecycle after this PR
diagrams.description: Shows how an XCTestCase suite moves through the async setUp and tearDown, with DependencyHelperMock providing shared test dependencies.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    runner[XCTest runner] --> setup["setUp() async throws"]
    setup --> sup1["try await super.setUp()"]
    sup1 --> boot[DependencyHelperMock.bootstrapDependencies]
    boot --> test[Test method]
    test --> td["tearDown() async throws"]
    td --> reset[DependencyHelperMock.reset]
    td --> sup2["try await super.tearDown()"]

findings.title: Removed @MainActor from EditBookmarkViewModelTests while it calls MainActor APIs
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Library/Bookmarks/EditBookmarkViewModelTests.swift`, the class-level `@MainActor` attribute was removed above `class EditBookmarkViewModelTests: XCTestCase` (line 11). The tests call `EditBookmarkViewModel.selectFolder(_:)`, which is `@MainActor` in `EditBookmarkViewModel.swift`, so the suite must be main-actor isolated. Restore `@MainActor` above the class declaration, matching the other suites changed in this PR such as `StoriesFeedDiffableDataSourceTests`. Leave the async `setUp`/`tearDown` as they are.

findings.title: XCTAssert replaced with Swift assert, so failures are not reported by XCTest
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Helpers/NotificationManagerTests.swift`, `testRequestAuthorization` (lines 25-30) now uses Swift `assert` instead of XCTest assertions. `assert` is compiled out in optimized builds and traps the test host rather than recording an XCTest failure. Restore `XCTAssertTrue` for the granted check and for the `requestAuthorizationWasCalled` check. `MockUserNotificationCenter` calls its completion synchronously, so the assertions can run inline or inside the closure as before. Match the style of `testGetNotificationSettings` in the same file, and drop the `[center]` capture if it is no longer needed.

findings.title: Inconsistent super.setUp / super.tearDown ordering
findings.body: The PR converts lifecycle methods to `try await super.setUp()` and `try await super.tearDown()`, but the placement is inconsistent. In `RatingPromptManagerTests`, `tearDown` calls `super.tearDown()` first, then does its cleanup. Most other suites in the PR call `super.tearDown()` last, which is the usual XCTest convention. The behavior is harmless here, but it is easy to make uniform while the lines are being touched.
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Helpers/RatingPromptManagerTests.swift`, `tearDown()` (around lines 36-46) calls `try await super.tearDown()` first and then does its cleanup. Move the `super.tearDown()` call to the end of the method so it matches the convention used by the other suites in this PR. Keep the cleanup statements unchanged.

findings.title: @unchecked Sendable on a mock with mutable state suppresses checks
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Mocks/MockUserNotificationCenter.swift`, the class declaration (line 9) is now `@unchecked Sendable` while holding mutable `var` state. Check how the mock is used across the test target. If it is only touched from the main actor, mark it `@MainActor` instead. If it must be used off the main actor, add a one-line comment explaining why `@unchecked` is safe. Do not change the mock's behavior.

findings.title: MockTabQueue signature now matches the protocol
findings.body: `MockTabQueue.getQueuedTabs(completion:)` is now `@MainActor @Sendable @escaping`, which matches the requirement in `Storage/Queue.swift` and the real `SQLiteQueue` implementation. Before this change the mock diverged from the protocol. The fix makes the mock a faithful test double.

findings.title: Consistent async setUp/tearDown migration
findings.body: Across the suites, the old `override func setUp()` and `tearDown()` become `async throws` overrides that call `super` explicitly. This is the concurrency-aware form XCTest supports, and it lets suites that now run on the main actor avoid extra isolation hops. `DependencyHelperMock` is not `@MainActor`, so calling it from the new lifecycle methods is safe.
